entries.subject: Hedman et al. Aegaeon measured axes
entries.finding: Hedman et al. (2020), Table 1 supplies semiaxes 0.70 ± 0.05, 0.25 ± 0.06 and 0.20 ± 0.08 km. The selected analytic ellipsoid approximates those dimensions; it is not a detailed irregular mesh.

entries.subject: Cassini Aegaeon 2010 sequence and 2015 candidate registration
entries.finding: The earlier N1643264167/N1829223369 check remained unregistered. Figure 18 and Table 27 reopen the route with N1643265020 and adjacent N1643264914: both native crops contain a diffuse disc candidate. Historical BPC/SPK combinations give N1643265020 viewing longitude 158.04–158.09 degrees west, near the paper's 158.3, whereas OPUS reports 291.756. This narrows the frame mismatch; it does not recover the producer's star-based image navigation or verify interior surface placement. Updated ephemerides and the 2015 frame were sampled without qualifying a camera. No photographic texels were promoted.
entries.revisitWhen: The producer's navigated image centre/attitude or an independently checked camera registration becomes available for the identified 2010 disc; validate interior placement on the fixed ellipsoid before preparation. Do not repeat the existence or longitude checks as if they were unresolved source retrieval.

entries.subject: PDS Saturn shape release for Aegaeon
entries.finding: The reviewed release did not provide a body-specific deliverable qualified for this package; the measured axes retain ownership of the approximation.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Aegaeon shape with usable frame and provenance can be reviewed.

entries.subject: Aegaeon terrain, colour and composition routes
entries.finding: Published photometry and spectra are integrated constraints, and no DEM, geology or mapped composition product was qualified.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially registered image, spectral, terrain or geology product can support a lens.
